params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The young man in the office chair looks up to the right, then sweeps his eyes across the room at his own eye level, right to left, pausing three times as if on three faces in front of him. His chest and shoulders rise in one slow breath and fall, mouth closed. He gives one small, decisive nod. He lifts one hand off the armrest, flicks two fingers forward once — go — and drops the hand back to the armrest. He swivels the chair round to the desk in one quick turn and puts both hands on the keyboard.

His mouth stays closed and his face stays the same calm face in every frame. The chair's base stays planted on the same spot of floor in every frame; only the seat turns. The three monitors stay dark, the same three dark screens with the same faint lines of code in every frame, and the desk and the cork board behind him stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
